newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans set contract high on demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans set contract high on demand.

text.p: CBOT July soybean futures notched a fresh contract high in fast dealings on fund buying amid ongoing concerns that strong demand would wipe out tight supplies, traders said.
The new high for the July is $8.94-1/2 per bushel, topping the previous high of $8.92-3/4 set on April 3 and the highest level since 1988.
Floor sources said stops were hit above Wednesday's high of $8.91 in the July. The move to new contract highs touched off another round of stops, they said.
Griffin Trading bought one million bushels July, pit sources said.

USDA's weekly export tally of 383,300 tonnes was the catalyst for the upward move, traders said. The export figure suggested price had not risen enough to ration world demand and renewed concerns that tight U.S. supplies would not last through the summer.
At 1229 CDT, soybeans were 8-3/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher with July up seven at $8.94.
